project.name: Three-Body Problem + CTL-PINN Training Stack
project.description: Complete simulation pipeline, metrics analysis, and Neural Network training stack for a three-body physics problem using the Brutus C++ arbitrary-precision integrator and Curriculum-Trained Physics-Informed Neural Networks.

nodes.name: datastructures.py
nodes.summary: Defines core data structures for dataset validation including validation status enums, issue tracking, file and dataset validation result containers, report aggregation, and Brutus result footer parsing.

nodes.name: ValidationStatus
nodes.summary: Enumeration defining validation status states (PASS, WARNING, FAIL) for validation checks.

nodes.name: ValidationIssue
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a single validation issue with severity, module, message, and location metadata.

nodes.name: FileValidationResult
nodes.summary: Container for validation results of a single file, tracking issues and providing overall status computation.

nodes.name: DatasetValidationResult
nodes.summary: Aggregates validation results for a dataset variant, tracking IC and Brutus results with methods to identify missing files.

nodes.name: ValidationReport
nodes.summary: Top-level validation report container with timestamp, configuration, dataset results, and summary statistics.

nodes.name: Snapshot
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a simulation snapshot with time, body count, CPU time, and particle states.

nodes.name: ResultFooter
nodes.summary: Dataclass parsing and validating Brutus result footer metadata including simulation parameters and energy conservation metrics.

nodes.name: create_issue
nodes.summary: Factory function creating ValidationIssue instances with standardized parameters for severity, module, message, and location.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package initialization importing all validation module functions for convenient access.

nodes.name: completeness.py
nodes.summary: Validates Brutus output file completeness by checking file size, parsing result footer, and verifying energy conservation and CPU time thresholds.

nodes.name: validate_completeness
nodes.summary: Validates Brutus file completeness by checking size, parsing footer, and verifying energy conservation and runtime thresholds.

nodes.name: coverage.py
nodes.summary: Validates IC file coverage by computing 13-component invariant vectors and checking for finite values and zero-energy configurations.

nodes.name: validate_coverage
nodes.summary: Validates IC file coverage by computing invariant vectors and checking for degenerate zero-energy configurations.

nodes.name: curriculum.py
nodes.summary: Validates curriculum stage assignment by computing physics invariants and checking stage boundaries against dataset quantiles.

nodes.name: assign_stage
nodes.summary: Assigns curriculum training stage based on energy, virial ratio, angular momentum, and dataset quantile boundaries.

nodes.name: validate_curriculum
nodes.summary: Validates curriculum stage assignment by computing physics invariants and checking stage boundaries.

nodes.name: file_format.py
nodes.summary: Validates IC and Brutus file formats including structure, column counts, numeric validity, and header/footer presence.

nodes.name: validate_ic_format
nodes.summary: Validates IC file format including existence, size, line count, column structure, numeric validity, and header/footer presence.

nodes.name: validate_brutus_format
nodes.summary: Validates Brutus output file format including timestep structure, particle data, numeric validity, and result footer presence.

nodes.name: metadata.py
nodes.summary: Validates Brutus file metadata by parsing result footer and checking simulation parameters against expected ranges.

nodes.name: validate_metadata
nodes.summary: Validates Brutus file metadata by parsing result footer and checking parameter ranges.

nodes.name: metrics.py
nodes.summary: Validates metrics JSON file structure and energy/momentum conservation values against expected thresholds.

nodes.name: validate_metrics
nodes.summary: Validates metrics JSON structure and conservation values against thresholds.

nodes.name: parameters.py
nodes.summary: Validates parameter file structure by checking timestep count and time range against expected values.

nodes.name: validate_parameters
nodes.summary: Validates parameter file structure by checking timestep count and time range consistency.

nodes.name: physics.py
nodes.summary: Validates IC physics properties including center of mass, total momentum, and energy conservation checks.

nodes.name: validate_ic_physics
nodes.summary: Validates IC physics by checking center of mass, momentum, and energy values.

nodes.name: temporal.py
nodes.summary: Validates temporal properties of Brutus output including timestep count, uniformity, and monotonicity.

nodes.name: validate_temporal
nodes.summary: Validates temporal properties including timestep count, uniformity, and monotonicity.

nodes.name: parsers.py
nodes.summary: Utility functions for parsing IC files, Brutus output files, and result footers, plus physics calculations for energy, center of mass, momentum, and angular momentum.

nodes.name: parse_ic_file
nodes.summary: Parses IC file extracting particle masses, positions, and velocities with validation.

nodes.name: parse_brutus_file
nodes.summary: Parses Brutus output file extracting snapshots with timestep metadata and particle states.

nodes.name: parse_result_footer
nodes.summary: Parses Brutus result footer line extracting simulation parameters and energy conservation metrics.

nodes.name: calculate_energy
nodes.summary: Calculates total energy (kinetic + potential) for a system of particles.

nodes.name: calculate_center_of_mass
nodes.summary: Calculates center of mass position for a system of particles.

nodes.name: calculate_total_momentum
nodes.summary: Calculates total linear momentum for a system of particles.

nodes.name: calculate_angular_momentum
nodes.summary: Calculates total angular momentum vector for a system of particles.

nodes.name: physics_core.py
nodes.summary: Core physics computation functions for invariant vectors including energy, angular momentum, moment of inertia, shape invariants, and velocity angles for curriculum staging.

nodes.name: compute_basic_invariants
nodes.summary: Computes basic physics invariants: kinetic energy, potential energy, total energy, min pairwise distance.

nodes.name: compute_angular_momentum_canonical
nodes.summary: Computes canonical angular momentum magnitude and characteristic scales for normalization.

nodes.name: compute_moment_of_inertia_normalized
nodes.summary: Computes normalized moment of inertia tensor and its trace for shape characterization.

nodes.name: compute_shape_invariants
nodes.summary: Computes sorted pairwise distance ratios as shape invariants for configuration characterization.

nodes.name: compute_velocity_angles
nodes.summary: Computes velocity angles (theta, phi) for each particle using spherical coordinate decomposition.

nodes.name: compute_13_component_vector
nodes.summary: Computes 13-component invariant vector combining energy, angular momentum, shape, velocity angles, and moment of inertia for curriculum classification.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package initializer for the dataset readiness checks suite. Re-exports the main Validator class, run_validation convenience function, global config singleton, and key datastructure types (ValidationReport, DatasetValidationResult, ValidationStatus) for external use.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the dataset readiness checks. Parses command-line arguments (variants, threshold, output-dir, modules, strict mode), invokes the validation pipeline, generates JSON and Markdown reports, and determines exit codes based on error/warning counts.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI arguments for variant selection, completeness threshold, output directory, module filtering, and strict mode. Runs validation, generates JSON and Markdown reports, and exits with code 0 (success), 1 (strict-mode warnings), or 2 (errors).

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central configuration management for the validation system. Defines the ValidationConfig dataclass with dataset variant mappings (4 IC/Brutus directory pairs), validation thresholds, file naming patterns, module enable/disable lists, and output settings. Provides YAML serialization and a global config singleton.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python dataclass with __post_init__ for lazy default initialization of mutable fields (dicts, lists, Paths). Global singleton instantiated at module level.

nodes.name: ValidationConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding all validation configuration: base paths, 4 dataset variant directory mappings, thresholds (completeness, energy, COM), filename patterns for IC and Brutus files, enabled validation modules list, and output settings. Includes accessor methods for variant-specific paths/patterns and YAML serialization.

nodes.name: blacklist.py
nodes.summary: Validation module that checks IC files against the problematic_ics_blacklist.json. Flags files that exist in the dataset but are blacklisted as errors (they should have been moved out). Maps gold variants to their base-type blacklist keys.

nodes.name: validate_against_blacklist
nodes.summary: Checks whether a given file number is in the blacklist for its variant. Returns an error issue if a blacklisted file exists in the dataset. Maps gold variants to their base blacklist keys (hierarchical/standard).

nodes.name: correspondence.py
nodes.summary: Validates 1:1 correspondence between IC files and Brutus output files for each dataset variant. Detects missing Brutus outputs, missing ICs, duplicate files, and handles blacklisted/excluded IDs (184 standard_gold exclusions parsed from documentation). Provides both issue-list and status-dictionary APIs.

nodes.name: validate_correspondence
nodes.summary: Main correspondence validation: extracts file numbers from IC and Brutus directories, checks for missing Brutus outputs (accounting for blacklisted ICs), missing ICs, and duplicates. Returns a list of ValidationIssue objects with appropriate severity levels.

nodes.name: is_blacklisted
nodes.summary: Checks if a file number is blacklisted for its variant. Handles both the problematic_ics_blacklist.json entries and the 184 standard_gold exclusion IDs from documentation. Maps gold variants to their base-type blacklist keys.

nodes.name: load_standard_gold_exclusions
nodes.summary: Parses standard_quasi_random_ids_not_in_gold.md to extract the 184 IC IDs that were not selected for gold-standard re-simulation. Parses code-fence blocks for numeric tokens. Warns if the count deviates from the expected 184.

nodes.name: check_for_duplicates
nodes.summary: Scans a directory for files matching the variant pattern and reports any numeric IDs that appear more than once as error-level issues.

nodes.name: log_summary
nodes.summary: Logs correspondence validation summary statistics: IC/Brutus file counts, missing outputs (with blacklisted count separated), completion percentage, and whether 1:1 correspondence is achieved. Handles standard_gold exclusion reporting.

nodes.name: get_correspondence_status
nodes.summary: Returns a detailed correspondence status dictionary for a variant including IC/Brutus counts, missing IDs (actual vs blacklisted), completion percentage, and perfect-correspondence flag. Wraps exceptions in an error dict.

nodes.name: json_report.py
nodes.summary: Generates JSON reports from validation results. Includes a custom JSON encoder (ReportEncoder) that handles Enum serialization by falling back to .value or str() conversion.

nodes.name: generate_json_report
nodes.summary: Converts a ValidationReport dataclass to JSON using asdict and a custom encoder that handles Enum values. Writes formatted JSON to the specified output path.

nodes.name: markdown.py
nodes.summary: Generates human-readable Markdown reports from validation results. Includes an executive summary with status counts, global issues section, and per-variant details with top-10 most frequent issues grouped by severity and message.

nodes.name: generate_markdown_report
nodes.summary: Writes a structured Markdown report with executive summary (total files, issues, dataset count), global issues list, and per-variant details including IC/Brutus counts, missing files, and top-10 issues sorted by occurrence count.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Utils package barrel file. Re-exports parser functions (parse_ic_file, parse_brutus_file, parse_result_footer, physics calculations), naming utilities (extract_file_numbers, get_filename_pattern, generate_filename, validate_filename_pattern), and logging utilities (ValidationLogger, setup_logging, get_logger).

nodes.name: logging.py
nodes.summary: Logging infrastructure for the validation system. Provides a singleton ValidationLogger with dual console/file handlers, severity-aware issue logging, TimedOperation context manager for operation timing, and a handle_validation_errors decorator for graceful error handling in validation modules.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses singleton pattern via __new__ with _initialized guard to ensure only one logger instance. File handler uses timestamp-based naming for log rotation.

nodes.name: ValidationLogger
nodes.summary: Singleton logger class providing centralized logging for the validation system. Configures dual console (INFO) and file (DEBUG) handlers on the 'three_body_validator' root logger. Provides domain-specific methods: log_validation_start, log_module_start, log_issue (maps ValidationStatus to log levels), and log_summary.

nodes.name: TimedOperation
nodes.summary: Context manager that times an operation and logs its duration on success or failure. Does not suppress exceptions.

nodes.name: handle_validation_errors
nodes.summary: Decorator that catches FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, and generic Exception in validation module functions, logs the error, and returns an empty issues list for graceful degradation.

nodes.name: naming.py
nodes.summary: Filename pattern handling utilities that bridge naming inconsistencies between directory names and actual file naming conventions. Provides functions to extract numeric IDs from directories, generate/validate filenames against variant-specific patterns, list matching files, and map directory names to standardized variant names.

nodes.name: extract_file_numbers
nodes.summary: Scans a directory for files matching IC or Brutus patterns for a given variant and extracts their numeric IDs into a set. Uses glob for pattern matching and regex for number extraction from filenames.

nodes.name: get_filename_pattern
nodes.summary: Returns the filename pattern string for a given variant and file type ('ic' or 'brutus') from the global config.

nodes.name: generate_filename
nodes.summary: Generates a concrete filename by formatting the variant/file_type pattern with the given numeric ID.

nodes.name: validate_filename_pattern
nodes.summary: Validates a filename against the expected pattern for a variant and file type. Returns the extracted numeric ID if valid, None otherwise. Checks prefix match and regex-based number extraction.

nodes.name: list_matching_files
nodes.summary: Lists all files in a directory matching the expected pattern for a variant and file type. Uses glob with prefix/suffix derived from the config pattern and double-checks prefix/suffix match on results.

nodes.name: map_directory_to_variant
nodes.summary: Maps raw directory names (e.g., 'ic_hierarchical', 'brutus_standard_quasi_random_gold_standard') to standardized variant names (e.g., 'hierarchical', 'standard_gold'). Returns None for unrecognized directories.

nodes.name: validator.py
nodes.summary: Main validation orchestrator. The Validator class dynamically loads 12 validation modules (correspondence, file_format, completeness, metadata, physics, parameters, metrics, blacklist, coverage, curriculum, temporal), iterates over IC and Brutus files per variant, dispatches each to the relevant modules, and aggregates results into DatasetValidationResult objects. Also provides a run_validation convenience function.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dynamic module loading in _load_modules() to avoid circular imports. Modules are dispatched by name from the config's enabled_modules list.

nodes.name: Validator
nodes.summary: Main orchestrator class that loads validation modules dynamically, validates IC and Brutus files per dataset variant by dispatching to enabled modules, runs correspondence validation, and aggregates results with summary statistics into DatasetValidationResult and ValidationReport objects.

nodes.name: run_validation
nodes.summary: Convenience function for quick validation runs. Creates a ValidationConfig, applies optional overrides (modules, threshold, output_dir), sets up logging, instantiates a Validator, and returns the aggregated ValidationReport.

nodes.name: Brutus.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the Brutus integrator class with arbitrary-precision arithmetic support, providing constructors for configurable tolerance, precision, and time-step parameters, plus methods for evolving N-body systems and retrieving state data.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses MPFR/GMP multi-precision types (mpreal) for arbitrary-precision arithmetic, with eta parameter auto-tuned from tolerance via logarithmic slope fitting.

nodes.name: Brutus.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the Brutus integrator class, including forward declarations for Bulirsch-Stoer stepper, Cluster, and Star types used in the N-body integration pipeline.

nodes.name: Bulirsch_Stoer.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the Bulirsch-Stoer semi-implicit integration method with polynomial extrapolation and adaptive error control for high-precision N-body orbital mechanics.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the Gragg modified midpoint method with Richardson extrapolation tableau and adaptive step sizing based on local truncation error estimation.

nodes.name: Bulirsch_Stoer.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the Bulirsch-Stoer integrator class with tolerance, step count, and extrapolation order parameters, plus integration and error control methods.

nodes.name: Cluster.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the Cluster class representing a gravitationally-bound N-body system, providing acceleration computation, position/velocity updates, energy calculation, and data serialization methods.
nodes.languageNotes: Computes pairwise Newtonian gravitational accelerations with softening, plus kinetic and potential energy via inner products for diagnostic output.

nodes.name: Cluster.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the Cluster class with Star vector storage, acceleration buffers, and methods for N-body force computation and time integration.

nodes.name: Star.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the Star class representing a single gravitating body with mass, position, and velocity vectors, including constructors for initialization from raw data.

nodes.name: Star.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the Star class with mass and 3D position/velocity vectors using arbitrary-precision mpreal types for high-fidelity N-body state representation.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: Entry point for the Brutus N-body integrator, handling command-line arguments, initial condition loading (from file or hardcoded test cases), precision setup, time evolution loop, and energy conservation diagnostics.
nodes.languageNotes: Supports multiple hardcoded initial conditions (figure-8, Sun-Earth-Moon, chaotic 3-body) plus file-based snapshot loading, with CPU timing and energy drift tracking.

nodes.name: evolve
nodes.summary: Advances the N-body system to a specified end time using the Bulirsch-Stoer integrator, iteratively computing accelerations and integrating until t_end is reached or an error occurs.

nodes.name: fit_slope
nodes.summary: Fits a linear model to log-log data points to determine the optimal eta (time-step scaling) parameter from tolerance, using least-squares regression on empirical precision-loss measurements.

nodes.name: Brutus
nodes.summary: Constructor initializing the Brutus integrator with default tolerance and precision, setting up the Bulirsch-Stoer stepper and internal state vectors.

nodes.name: Brutus
nodes.summary: Constructor accepting initial time, state data, and tolerance, automatically computing eta and precision bits from the tolerance parameter.

nodes.name: Brutus
nodes.summary: Constructor accepting initial time, state data, tolerance, and explicit bit precision, with eta auto-computed from tolerance.

nodes.name: Brutus
nodes.summary: Constructor accepting initial time, state data, tolerance, bit precision, and explicit eta parameter for full manual control of integration settings.

nodes.name: Brutus
nodes.summary: Constructor accepting all integration parameters including nmax (maximum extrapolation order) for advanced configuration of the Bulirsch-Stoer stepper.

nodes.name: get_eta
nodes.summary: Computes the eta parameter (time-step scaling factor) from tolerance using a piecewise function with empirical breakpoints, ensuring stable integration across precision regimes.

nodes.name: get_data_double
nodes.summary: Serializes the current N-body state (positions and velocities) to a vector of double-precision floats for output or analysis.

nodes.name: get_data_string
nodes.summary: Serializes the current N-body state to a vector of strings with full arbitrary-precision representation for high-fidelity output.

nodes.name: integrate
nodes.summary: Main integration loop that advances the Cluster state by one macro time-step dt, calling the step function and handling step rejection/retry on error control failure.

nodes.name: step
nodes.summary: Performs one Bulirsch-Stoer step using the modified midpoint method with increasing subdivision counts, building the extrapolation tableau and applying error control to determine step acceptance.

nodes.name: extrapol
nodes.summary: Performs polynomial extrapolation on the Gragg sequence of midpoint solutions to estimate the exact solution at dt, updating the state and derivative vectors.

nodes.name: extrapolate
nodes.summary: Helper function performing rational or polynomial extrapolation for a single value using the Neville-Aitken algorithm on the extrapolation tableau.

nodes.name: error_control
nodes.summary: Computes the weighted RMS error between two extrapolation estimates and determines whether the step meets the tolerance criterion, returning a boolean acceptance flag.

nodes.name: Bulirsch_Stoer
nodes.summary: Constructor initializing the Bulirsch-Stoer integrator with tolerance and system size N, allocating internal buffers for the extrapolation tableau.

nodes.name: Bulirsch_Stoer
nodes.summary: Constructor accepting tolerance, maximum extrapolation order n_max, maximum subdivision k_max, and system size N for full manual configuration.

nodes.name: calcAcceleration_dt
nodes.summary: Computes gravitational accelerations and their time derivatives for all stars in the cluster using direct N-body summation with Newton's third law optimization and optional softening.

nodes.name: calcAcceleration
nodes.summary: Computes gravitational accelerations only (without time derivatives) for all stars using direct pairwise summation, used in the leapfrog-style integration scheme.

nodes.name: Cluster
nodes.summary: Constructor initializing a Cluster from a flat data vector containing mass, position, and velocity for each star, allocating acceleration and energy buffers.

nodes.name: Cluster
nodes.summary: Alternative constructor initializing a Cluster from a data vector with explicit Star object construction, providing the same functionality with different data layout assumptions.

nodes.name: energies
nodes.summary: Computes total kinetic and potential energy of the cluster, returning both values for energy conservation diagnostics during integration.

nodes.name: get_data_double
nodes.summary: Serializes the cluster state (mass, positions, velocities for all stars) to a flat vector of double-precision floats for output or interoperability.

nodes.name: get_data
nodes.summary: Serializes the cluster state to a flat vector of arbitrary-precision mpreal values, preserving full precision for high-fidelity data output.

nodes.name: Star
nodes.summary: Default constructor initializing a Star with zero mass, position, and velocity vectors.

nodes.name: Star
nodes.summary: Constructor initializing a Star with specified mass, position, and velocity vectors from input data.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that parses command-line arguments, loads initial conditions, sets up arbitrary-precision arithmetic, runs the Brutus integrator to evolve the N-body system, and outputs final state with energy conservation metrics.

nodes.name: get_initial_condition
nodes.summary: Provides hardcoded initial conditions for various N-body test problems including figure-8 orbit, Sun-Earth-Moon system, and chaotic three-body configurations, returning flat state vectors.

nodes.name: calculate_total_energy
nodes.summary: Computes the total energy (kinetic + potential) of an N-body system from a flat state vector, used for monitoring energy conservation during integration.

nodes.name: read_snapshot_from_file
nodes.summary: Reads an N-body snapshot from a text file, parsing mass, position, and velocity for each body into a flat state vector for initialization.

nodes.name: MyPrint
nodes.summary: Formats and prints simulation output including time, CPU time, and N-body state data with configurable precision for diagnostic logging.

nodes.name: metrics_analysis.py
nodes.summary: Provides three high-level plotting functions for simulation metrics: histograms of simulation times, heatmaps of initial separation vs duration, and scatter plots of IC type vs energy error. Consumes metrics files produced by the Brutus pipeline and delegates parsing to utils.load_metrics.

nodes.name: particle_positions_viz.py
nodes.summary: Generates comprehensive visualizations of hierarchical three-body initial conditions: 3D scatter overviews, hierarchical property distributions, example systems, particle role analysis (binary vs distant), and configuration-space projections. Orchestrated by a main() entry point that loads a dataset, computes statistics, and dispatches to individual plot builders.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Shared utilities for the Validation/analysis module: parses Brutus IC files (positions/velocities/masses), loads metric files in both JSON and legacy text formats, calculates hierarchical three-body properties (binary separations, hierarchy ratios, COM distances, distant-particle flags), and provides stratified/random file sampling helpers for large datasets.

nodes.name: histogram_simulation_times
nodes.summary: Walks a directory of metrics files, extracts per-simulation wall-clock times via utils.load_metrics, and renders a histogram of simulation durations with configurable display.

nodes.name: heatmap_pos2_vs_duration
nodes.summary: Produces a hexbin heatmap of initial second-body position magnitude vs. simulation duration across a metrics directory, using log-scaled color normalization to handle heavy-tailed timing distributions.

nodes.name: scatter_ic_vs_energy
nodes.summary: Scatter-plots IC type (categorized by filename suffix) against relative energy error for every simulation in a directory, exposing systematic energy-conservation failures by initial-condition class.

nodes.name: analyze_hierarchical_dataset
nodes.summary: Loads a sample of hierarchical IC files from a directory, parses positions, and computes hierarchical properties (binary separations, ratios, COM distances, distant-particle flags) for each system. Returns arrays aggregated across the sample.

nodes.name: create_3d_scatter_overview
nodes.summary: Builds a 4-panel figure of 3D scatter plots showing particle positions (XYZ, XY, XZ, YZ projections) for the full hierarchical dataset, with per-particle color coding.

nodes.name: create_hierarchical_properties_plot
nodes.summary: Plots histograms of binary separations, hierarchy ratios, and COM distances plus a separation-vs-ratio scatter, summarizing the geometric distribution of the hierarchical dataset.

nodes.name: create_example_systems_plot
nodes.summary: Selects representative example systems at percentile-sampled binary separations and renders their 3D particle configurations, with binary pairs connected by line segments to highlight the hierarchical structure.

nodes.name: create_particle_role_analysis
nodes.summary: Analyzes the 'distant third body' role in hierarchical triples: bar chart of distant-particle counts per system, plus overlaid histograms of distance-from-origin for distant vs binary particles.

nodes.name: create_configuration_space_plot
nodes.summary: Projects the dataset into configuration space: binary-relative-vector scatter colored by separation, histogram of inter-vector angles, position-vs-velocity magnitude scatter, and velocity-space scatter.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that analyzes the default hierarchical IC directory, prints dataset statistics (size, mean/min/max separations and ratios), creates the output directory, and dispatches all five plot builders.

nodes.name: parse_ic_file
nodes.summary: Reads a Brutus initial-condition file and returns position (Nx3) and velocity (Nx3) numpy arrays by parsing whitespace-delimited rows of six floats per particle.

nodes.name: load_ic_file
nodes.summary: Extends parse_ic_file to also extract per-particle masses from the first column of the IC file, returning (positions, velocities, masses) as numpy arrays.

nodes.name: parse_metric_file
nodes.summary: Parses the legacy whitespace-delimited metric text format (key-value pairs, with multi-word keys joined by underscores) into a flat dictionary of floats. Falls back to substring matching when no '=' separator is present.

nodes.name: load_metrics
nodes.summary: Loads a single simulation's metrics from either JSON or legacy text format, normalizing the output into a dict with timing, energy conservation, hierarchy classification, IC file stem, and (when the paired IC file can be located) parsed positions. Infers hierarchy type from filename suffixes and reconciles metric/IC case numbers.

nodes.name: load_metrics_with_positions
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around load_metrics that supplies an explicit IC base directory, ensuring position parsing is attempted even when the metrics file lives outside the IC tree.

nodes.name: calculate_hierarchical_properties
nodes.summary: Given 3-body positions (3x3), identifies the tightest binary pair, computes its separation, the hierarchy ratio (inner/outer), center-of-mass distance of the binary from the origin, and a boolean flag for whether the third body is 'distant' (exceeds a separation-based threshold).

nodes.name: get_sample_files
nodes.summary: Samples IC files from a directory using one of three strategies (random, stratified-by-decade, stratified-by-quartile). The stratified strategies bin files by an embedded numeric key (e.g., energy or separation) and draw proportional samples per stratum to preserve distributional shape.

nodes.name: sample_files
nodes.summary: Simpler stratified sampler: bins IC files by an embedded numeric key into n_strata equal-count strata, draws samples_per_stratum from each, and returns the combined selection. A leaner alternative to get_sample_files without decade/quartile variants.

nodes.name: gemini-dispatch.yml
nodes.summary: Entry-point GitHub Actions workflow that routes PR/issue/comment events to the appropriate Gemini sub-workflow (review, triage, or invoke) based on event type, author association, and @gemini-cli trigger mentions. Includes a debug job and a fallthrough job that posts guidance when no sub-workflow matches.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses GitHub Actions reusable workflow calls (`workflow_call`) to delegate to sibling workflows; concurrency groups and conditional dispatch via `if` expressions on event payloads.

nodes.name: gemini-invoke.yml
nodes.summary: Reusable workflow invoked by the dispatcher that runs the Gemini CLI against an issue or PR with additional context, minting a GitHub App identity token for authenticated writes back to the issue/PR thread.

nodes.name: gemini-review.yml
nodes.summary: Reusable workflow that checks out the repository and runs the Gemini CLI to perform an AI-assisted pull request review, posting review comments back to the PR.

nodes.name: gemini-scheduled-triage.yml
nodes.summary: Hourly scheduled workflow that scans the repository for unlabelled issues, uses Gemini to classify them against the repository's label set, and applies the selected labels via a second labelling job.
nodes.languageNotes: Triggered by cron, push/PR to main/release branches (when the workflow file itself changes), and manual `workflow_dispatch`; paginates the repository label list via `github.paginate.iterator`.

nodes.name: gemini-triage.yml
nodes.summary: Reusable workflow that uses the Gemini CLI to select appropriate labels for a single issue or PR given its title, body, and the repository's available labels, returning the selected labels as a workflow output for downstream labelling.

nodes.name: gemini-invoke.toml
nodes.summary: Defines the Gemini CLI prompt for the autonomous AI software engineering agent invoked by a GitHub Actions workflow. It prescribes a structured Plan -> Approve -> Execute -> Report cycle, with strict security constraints (treat external input as untrusted, no direct execution, no command substitution) and mandatory tool-based GitHub interactions.

nodes.name: gemini-review.toml
nodes.summary: Defines the Gemini CLI prompt for the autonomous code-review agent that reviews pull requests inside a GitHub Actions workflow. It enforces a three-step workflow (Data Gathering, Formulate Review Comments, Submit Pending Review), requires severity-tagged comments aligned precisely to diff lines, and restricts all output to MCP-tool-based GitHub interactions.

nodes.name: gemini-scheduled-triage.toml
nodes.summary: Defines the Gemini CLI prompt for scheduled batch issue triage. The agent parses a list of issues and available labels from environment variables, builds a semantic label map, and writes a minified JSON array of triage decisions (issue_number, labels_to_set, explanation) back to $GITHUB_ENV for downstream workflow consumption.

nodes.name: gemini-triage.toml
nodes.summary: Defines the Gemini CLI prompt for single-issue triage invoked from a GitHub Actions workflow. It classifies one issue against an available-labels list and appends a SELECTED_LABELS CSV to $GITHUB_ENV for downstream steps to consume.

nodes.name: MILESTONES.md
nodes.summary: Records all shipped milestones (v1.0 through v1.4) with their phase counts, plan counts, task counts, and key accomplishments. Serves as the historical ledger of project delivery.

nodes.name: PROJECT.md
nodes.summary: Defines the project scope, core value proposition (simulation dataset and data pipeline correctness), key decisions, validated requirements, and source-of-truth references for the Three-Body Physics-Informed LLM project.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the project README to understand the complete Three-Body Problem + CTL-PINN Training Stack. This document provides the architecture overview, repository map, prerequisites, 5-stage quickstart runbook, dataset layout conventions, and data quality checks. It establishes the mental model for the entire simulation pipeline: IC generation → Brutus integration → metrics calculation → prescreening → validation → PINN training.

tour.title: Data Pipeline Entry Point
tour.description: The IC (Initial Conditions) generation script is Stage 1 of the data pipeline. This CLI entry point delegates to the continuation-enhanced IC generation logic in ic_generation_utils. It produces the initial conditions that will be fed into the Brutus integrator. Understanding this entry point reveals how the pipeline begins: Sobol-sampled quasi-Monte Carlo three-body systems are generated with hierarchical stability guarantees.

tour.title: IC Generation Core Library
tour.description: The ic_generation_utils module is the computational heart of Stage 1. It provides Sobol-sampled quasi-Monte Carlo three-body initial conditions, hierarchical stable system generation, invariant computation (energy, angular momentum), and continuation-aware batch production. This library ensures that generated ICs satisfy physical constraints and statistical properties required for the training dataset. The utilities here are referenced by the entry point and form the foundation for all downstream simulation work.

tour.title: Brutus N-Body Integrator
tour.description: Brutus is the C++ arbitrary-precision N-body integration engine at the core of the simulation stack. The main.cpp entry point handles command-line arguments, IC loading, precision setup, and the time evolution loop with energy conservation diagnostics. Brutus.h declares the integrator class with forward declarations for the Bulirsch-Stoer stepper, Cluster, and Star types. Cluster.cpp implements the gravitationally-bound N-body system with acceleration computation and data serialization. Star.cpp represents individual gravitating bodies with mass, position, and velocity vectors. This is where the physics happens: arbitrary-precision arithmetic ensures numerical stability for the chaotic three-body problem.
tour.languageLesson: C++ arbitrary-precision arithmetic (via GMP/MPFR libraries) allows Brutus to control numerical error accumulation over long integration times. The Bulirsch-Stoer semi-implicit method with polynomial extrapolation provides adaptive step sizes, critical for handling the close encounters common in three-body dynamics.

tour.title: Batch Simulation Runner
tour.description: The batch runner orchestrates execution of the Brutus integrator across the entire IC dataset. It invokes Brutus for both hierarchical and standard IC directories, validates outputs, and quarantines problematic runs. This script bridges the gap between single-system integration (Brutus) and大规模 dataset generation, handling the practical concerns of batch processing: error handling, output validation, and result management. The runner ensures that only valid simulation trajectories proceed to metrics calculation.

tour.title: Metrics Calculation Pipeline
tour.description: After Brutus completes integration, the metrics calculation pipeline computes conservation-law drifts (energy, angular momentum), separation statistics, hierarchical-structure detection, and escape/collision classification. It persists per-IC JSON summaries that characterize each simulation's physical properties and numerical quality. These metrics form the basis for dataset quality assessment and prescreening decisions. The pipeline transforms raw trajectory data into physically meaningful features that the PINN will learn to predict.

tour.title: Stage 2 Prescreening
tour.description: The Stage 2 prescreening pipeline applies revised threshold criteria to filter initial conditions based on simulation quality metrics. It supports incremental processing and resumable checkpoints, allowing large datasets to be processed reliably. This stage removes ICs that produced numerically unstable or physically uninteresting trajectories, ensuring that only high-quality data enters the training set. The prescreening criteria are tuned to balance dataset size against physical diversity and numerical accuracy.

tour.title: Dataset Validation Framework
tour.description: The dataset readiness checks form a comprehensive validation pipeline that verifies the integrity and quality of the generated simulation data. The __main__.py CLI entry point parses arguments and invokes the validation pipeline, generating JSON and Markdown reports. The datastructures.py module (with fan-in of 16, the most depended-on file in the validation subsystem) defines core data structures: validation status enums, issue tracking, file and dataset validation result containers, report aggregation, and Brutus result footer parsing. This validation layer ensures that the dataset meets all requirements before being used for PINN training.

tour.title: PINN Architecture Specification
tour.description: The PINN architecture specification defines the Physics-Informed Neural Network structure that will learn to predict three-body dynamics from the simulation dataset. This framework spec (part of the v1.4 adjudication milestone) establishes the network architecture, automatic differentiation contract, and output head design. It represents the machine learning counterpart to the physics simulation pipeline: where Brutus solves the forward problem (ICs → trajectories), the PINN learns the inverse mapping. The specification is authoritative for the FUT-01 rewrite phase that will construct the training code from these specs.

tour.title: Curriculum Training Methodology
tour.description: The CTL (Curriculum Training Learning) instruction specification defines the training methodology for the PINN. Curriculum training progressively increases task difficulty, allowing the network to learn simple patterns before tackling complex chaotic dynamics. This specification covers the input-vector formulation, curriculum staging, and training routines. The methodology addresses a key challenge in learning chaotic systems: without curriculum training, the network may fail to converge on the complex long-term behaviors characteristic of the three-body problem. This spec, together with pinn_architecture.md and sampling_method.md, forms the complete PINN framework specification triad.

tour.title: Initial Condition Sampling Method
tour.description: The sampling method specification defines how initial conditions are generated for the training dataset. It covers the Sobol quasi-Monte Carlo sampling strategy, hierarchical stability criteria, and invariant-preserving transformations. This spec is the authoritative source for the IC generation logic implemented in ic_generation_utils.py (Stage 1 of the pipeline). The sampling strategy ensures statistical coverage of the three-body phase space while maintaining physical validity. The specification was revised during v1.4 to clarify the Jacobi state IC contract and remove legacy invariant/mass-fraction wording.

tour.title: Agent Governance and Workflow
tour.description: The AGENTS.md file is the canonical instruction set for all AI coding agents working in this repository. It defines the v1.4 adjudication governance model, including the STOP protocol for source-silent decisions (agents must halt and surface gaps rather than invent content), git branch awareness and commit protocol, and authoritative source-of-truth file listings. The governance model reflects a key project principle: spec engineering and physics adjudication decisions require explicit user instruction and cannot be delegated to agents. CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md symlink to this file, ensuring consistent agent behavior across different AI tools.
